title: Question 2

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Determine the direction of the uniform magnetic field.
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 2.2 from above and focus on the sphere position - which way is it moving and which way must the force on it point to keep it on that 3.4 m circle?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find velocity and centre-seeking direction**
Think of yourself looking down on the circle. At the sphere position the tangent shows the instantaneous velocity in the horizontal plane, and the force needed to bend it into a circle must point horizontally toward the centre of the circle.

Step 2: **Apply Fleming's left-hand rule**
For a positive charge, first finger is field $B$, second finger is current or velocity $v$, thumb is force $F$. With $v$ in the horizontal plane and $F$ toward the centre in the horizontal plane, the only $B$ direction that is perpendicular to both and satisfies $F = qvB$ is vertical. Checking the sense gives $B$ vertically downwards, into the plane of motion.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the motion of the sphere in the horizontal plane is circular.

markscheme_points.text: magnetic force (on sphere) is perpendicular to its velocity or magnetic force perpendicular to velocity is the centripetal force or magnetic force perpendicular to velocity causes centripetal acceleration or acceleration perpendicular to velocity is centripetal (acceleration) or magnetic force does not change the speed of the sphere or magnetic force has constant magnitude

hints: Hint 1: Recall the angle between the magnetic force $F = qvB\sin\theta$ and the velocity for a charge moving perpendicular to a uniform field.
Hint 2: Think about what a force that is always at 90 degrees to motion and always constant in size does to speed and to direction.
parts.proper_answer: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity and of constant magnitude. It therefore acts as the centripetal force, changing direction but not speed, giving uniform circular motion.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Direction of the magnetic force**
The magnetic force on a moving charge is given by $$F = Bqv\sin\theta$$ and its direction is perpendicular to both $B$ and $v$. Here $v$ is horizontal and $B$ is vertical, so $F$ stays in the horizontal plane and is always at $90^{\circ}$ to $v$.

Step 2: **Why this means a circle**
A force always perpendicular to velocity does no work, so speed $v$ stays constant at $0.78\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $F = Bqv$ stays constant in magnitude. A constant-magnitude force always perpendicular to motion is exactly the condition for centripetal force, so it continuously bends the path toward the centre and produces uniform circular motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the strength of the uniform electric field.
hints: Hint 1: The sphere stays at a fixed vertical height, so think about which two vertical forces must cancel - weight acting down and the electric force acting up.
Hint 2: Write the balance as an equation linking $m$, $g$, $E$ and $q$, then check that $q = 0.27\text{ nC}$ is converted to coulombs before rearranging for $E$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Balance weight with electric force**
Weight acts down: $W = mg$. Electric force on a positive charge acts in the direction of $E$, so up: $F = Eq$. For fixed height there is no resultant vertical force, so $$mg = Eq$$

Step 2: **Calculate E**
Rearrange before substituting: $$E = \frac{mg}{q}$$ Use $m = 1.6 \times 10^{-10}\text{ kg}$, $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $q = 0.27\text{ nC} = 0.27 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}$: $$E = \frac{(1.6 \times 10^{-10})(9.81)}{0.27 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 5.8\text{ N C}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: By considering the magnetic force on the sphere, show that the flux density of the uniform magnetic field is $0.14 \text{T}$.

markscheme_points.text: centripetal force = magnetic force or Bqv = mv^2 / r

hints: Hint 1: In the horizontal plane the only bending force is magnetic, so think about equating the magnetic expression $Bqv$ to the circular-motion expression for centripetal force.
Hint 2: Rearrange that equality symbolically to make magnetic flux density $B$ the subject in terms of $m$, $v$, $q$ and $r$.
Hint 3: Substitute $m = 1.6 \times 10^{-10}\text{ kg}$, $v = 0.78\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $q = 0.27 \times 10^{-9}\text{ C}$ and $r = 3.4\text{ m}$, and check the unit gives tesla.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Set magnetic force equal to required centripetal force**
Circular motion at speed $v$ and radius $r$ needs: $$F_{c} = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}$$ This is provided by the magnetic force with $v$ perpendicular to $B$: $$F_{B} = Bqv$$ Hence: $$Bqv = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}$$

Step 2: **Rearrange for B**
Cancel one $v$: $$B = \frac{mv}{qr}$$ This shows $B$ depends only on momentum, charge and radius.

Step 3: **Substitute and show 0.14 T**
$$B = \frac{(1.6 \times 10^{-10})(0.78)}{(0.27 \times 10^{-9})(3.4)}$$ Numerator $= 1.248 \times 10^{-10}$, denominator $= 9.18 \times 10^{-10}$, so $$B \approx 0.136\text{ T} \approx 0.14\text{ T}$$ as required.
